topic: Word Usage (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Word Usage
sections.content: Word Usage refers to understanding whether a word is used correctly in a sentence. Many English words can function both as nouns and verbs. It is important to identify the correct meaning and grammatical role of the word according to the sentence.

sections.title: Word as Noun vs Verb
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the word is naming a person, place, thing, or idea (noun). Step 2: Check whether the same word is showing an action (verb). Step 3: Identify the correct role based on the sentence structure. Example: 'I had a long run in the morning.' Here 'run' is a noun. 'I run every morning.' Here 'run' is a verb.

sections.title: Context-Based Word Meaning
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of the entire sentence. Step 2: Check whether the word logically fits the context. Step 3: If the meaning of the word does not match the context, the usage is incorrect. Example: 'He drank a glass of bread.' Here the word 'bread' is incorrect because drinking normally relates to liquids.

sections.title: Simple Word Misuse Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the main verb and noun of the sentence. Step 2: Check whether the word belongs to the correct grammatical category. Step 3: Verify both grammar and meaning. Example: 'She gave me a good advise.' Here 'advise' is a verb, while the correct noun form should be 'advice'.

sections.title: Common Confusing Words
sections.content: Some words have similar spellings but different meanings. Example: Advice (noun) and Advise (verb), Practice (noun) and Practise (verb), Use (noun/verb). It is important to recognize their correct usage.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not recognizing the difference between noun and verb forms. 2. Choosing a word that does not match the context. 3. Confusing words with similar spellings.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Word Usage questions, identifying the correct grammatical role and context is essential. First understand the sentence meaning, then determine whether the word is a noun or a verb, and finally check whether its usage is logical.

tricks.title: Position Check Trick
tricks.explanation: If a word comes after an article (a, an, the), it is usually a noun.

tricks.title: Verb Action Trick
tricks.explanation: If a word shows an action, it is likely a verb.

tricks.title: Sentence Meaning Check
tricks.explanation: Read the whole sentence and check whether the word fits the context logically.
tricks.example: He drank water (correct), He drank bread (incorrect).

tricks.title: Advice vs Advise Trick
tricks.explanation: Advice is a noun and Advise is a verb.
tricks.example: She gave good advice. He advised me to study.

tricks.title: Practice vs Practise Trick
tricks.explanation: Practice is a noun and Practise is a verb (British usage).

tricks.title: Article Clue Trick
tricks.explanation: A verb generally does not come immediately after an article.
tricks.example: A run is good for health.

tricks.title: Context Replacement Trick
tricks.explanation: Replace the word with a similar meaning word to check if the sentence still makes sense.
tricks.example: He gave advice → He gave suggestion.

tricks.title: Noun Ending Clue
tricks.explanation: Certain endings indicate nouns, such as -ment, -tion, and -ness.
